title: Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds
summary: Whole-roadmap plan of Deligne’s Weil I and Weil II theorems over the two accepted parts (DWP.0–DWP.6 with DWP.10, and DWP.7–DWP.9). It applies the accepted ownership transfer to EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.7 (2026-10-14): 65 part targets, the weight foundations EDC.7’s decomposition theorem needs, are retired here and imported from EDC.7, and the 70 surviving targets are imported with their prerequisites repointed and their text corrected. It moves down the 13 citations of WeilConjectures and FunctionFieldArithmetic, which lie outside the upstream order, as six new targets: rationality descent and Fatou, weight separation of zeta factors (both transferred from RD.7 as its assembly proposed), Weil I Theorem 1.6, point-count bounds, purity of smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stacks and the curve Chebotarev theorem. All 95 items of the four maintainer-added sources are accounted for, and the confirmed findings RT-AREA-etale/1 and /9 are handled. All eleven stages are planned; one new gap (Weil II 3.3.11 on algebraic spaces) is recorded; nothing is implemented.
granularity: Target level (PROTOCOL.md section 2). The accepted same-roadmap part targets are imported by id and corrected through the assembly record; they are not repeated as nodes, because a node id may live in one packet of a roadmap only.

hypotheses: q > 1 is needed for the weights to separate eigenvalues (EDC.7/weight-weil-q-number).
Equal weights allow non-split extensions (the Jordan block) and nonzero maps.
proofSteps: Coprimality: two polynomials with no common root in Ē are coprime (mathlib:Polynomial.isCoprime_iff_aeval_ne_zero_of_isAlgClosed). Write aP_F + bP_G = 1.

Cayley–Hamilton: P_F(F) = 0 (mathlib:LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly). From uF = Gu we get 0 = uP_F(F) = P_F(G)u. Since a(G)P_F(G) = 1 − b(G)P_G(G) = 1, P_F(G) is invertible, and u = 0. No extension of scalars is needed.
Different weights give disjoint eigenvalue sets, by uniqueness of the weight (EDC.7/weight-weil-q-number, q > 1) or of the ι-weight.

(ii): with P_n and P_m the characteristic polynomials of W and V/W, V = ker P_n(F) ⊕ ker P_m(F) (mathlib:Polynomial.sup_ker_aeval_eq_ker_aeval_mul_of_coprime and Cayley–Hamilton). ker P_n(F) contains W and has the same dimension, so ker P_m(F) is an F-stable complement. It is unique, because an F-stable complement is isomorphic to V/W, hence annihilated by P_m(F).

hypotheses: (i) holds over E itself. P_n has coefficients in E because Aut(Ē/E) permutes the eigenvalues, preserving multiplicities and Weil weights, and E is perfect.

(ii) does not descend to E in general, because the ι-weight is not Galois-invariant. Take E = ℚ and F with characteristic polynomial T² − 2T − 1 (eigenvalues 1 ± √2). For every ι it has the two distinct ι-weights ±2 log₂(1 + √2) relative to 2, but no F-stable line over ℚ.
Each V_n need not be semisimple.

Separating the factors of a zeta function, with their integrality and ℓ-independence, is DWP.0/weight-separated-factor-extraction, applied to smooth projective varieties in DWP.4/integral-cohomological-factors. This node decomposes one Frobenius module.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.2/weights-an.statement: On an open U₀⊂ℙ¹ over 𝔽_q, specialize EDC.7’s common punctual purity predicate (EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness) to a lisse ℚ_ℓ-sheaf ℱ₀: integer weight β means each closed-point stalk is pure β relative to q^(deg x). The local determinant and Euler product are the SF.2 coefficient L-function, with local variable t^(deg x). Changing geometric stalk conjugates Frobenius and leaves its determinant unchanged; tensor weights add, dual weights negate, and the Tate line ℚ_ℓ(r) has weight −2r. This comparison fixes the inputs of Weil I §3 without defining a second purity predicate or L-function.
proofSteps: Use the common closed-stalk definition and geometric-Frobenius convention. Coefficient-extension invariance identifies the ℚ_ℓ model with its algebraic closure.
Import local characteristic-polynomial conjugacy invariance and the Euler determinant formula from SF.2. Apply the numeric tensor, dual and Tate identities to the stalks.
hypotheses: This is Weil I (3.1): all complex conjugates of the Frobenius eigenvalues, that is, Weil q_x-numbers. EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness generalizes it to Weil II's pointwise purity on schemes of finite type and to real ι-weights, and must identify its predicate with this one on open subsets of ℙ¹.
F₀ has a fixed ℚ_ℓ-model, as RS-17 keeps. ℚ̄_ℓ enters only through the eigenvalues.
The geometric Frobenius is used (the conventions of EDC.7/weight-endomorphism-weights).

proofSteps: Reduce to U affine and F₀ ≠ 0.

Fix x of degree d and an eigenvalue α of F_x on F₀. By (iii), α is algebraic and every complex conjugate of α is again an eigenvalue. α^{2k} is an eigenvalue of F_x on ⊗^{2k}F₀ (EDC.7/weight-spectra-of-tensor-products-and-duals). So the local factor det(1 − F_x t^d, ⊗^{2k}F₀)⁻¹ has a pole at every t with t^d = α^{−2k}.

That local factor is one factor of Z(U₀, ⊗^{2k}F₀, t) = ∏_y (local factor at y). All the factors have nonnegative coefficients (EDC.7/weight-positive-euler-product-comparison), and Z is rational with poles only at q^{−kβ−1} (theorem compact-cohomology-of-even-tensor-powers). The pole comparison of EDC.7/weight-positive-euler-product-comparison gives |α|^{−2k/d} ≥ q^{−kβ−1}, that is, |α| ≤ q_x^{β/2 + 1/(2k)}.
Letting k → ∞ gives |α| ≤ q_x^{β/2}.

ψ is Frobenius-equivariant with values in ℚ_ℓ(−β), on which F_x acts by q_x^β. So q_x^β/α is also an eigenvalue (EDC.7/weight-reciprocal-pairing-of-eigenvalues with c = q_x^β), and the previous step applied to it gives |α| ≥ q_x^{β/2}. The same argument applies to every complex conjugate of α.

The exact sequence 0 → j_!F → j_*F → j_*F/j_!F → 0 has a punctual third term, so H¹_c(U, F) → H¹(ℙ¹, j_*F) is surjective. Every α is therefore an eigenvalue on H¹_c(U, F), and Corollary 3.8 gives |α| ≤ q^{β/2+1}.

Poincaré duality (2.12) pairs H¹(ℙ¹, j_*F) with H¹(ℙ¹, j_*F^∨(1)) into ℚ_ℓ, and ψ identifies F^∨ with F(β). So q^{β+1}/α is an eigenvalue (EDC.7/weight-reciprocal-pairing-of-eigenvalues), and |q^{β+1}α⁻¹| ≤ q^{β/2+1} gives |α| ≥ q^{β/2}.

d(1−π^m)=1 at the origin, so 1−π^m is étale. Properness and a zero-dimensional kernel make it a finite surjective isogeny. Its geometric kernel is A(𝔽_(q^m)), with multiplicity one. Hence #A(𝔽_(q^m))=deg(1−π^m)=P_(π^m)(1), using the A6 isogeny degree and characteristic-polynomial contracts.
The eigenvalues of π^m are the a_i^m (EDC.7/weight-spectra-of-polynomials-in-an-endomorphism), so P_{π^m}(1) = ∏(1 − a_i^m).

Expand ∏(1 − a_i^m): the term ∏a_i^m = q^{mg}; the 2g terms that are products of 2g − 1 roots have absolute value q^{m(g−1/2)}; the remaining 2^{2g} − 2g − 1 terms have absolute value at most q^{m(g−1)} (Weil estimate).
Zeta function: log Z = Σ N_m t^m/m with N_m = Σ_r (−1)^r Tr(π^m | ∧^r), and the eigenvalues of π on ∧^r T_ℓA are the r-fold products (EDC.7/weight-eigenvalues-of-exterior-powers).
The Frobenius of V ⊗ 𝔽_{q^m} is π_V^m (the q-Frobenius of SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/absolute-frobenius, property (e)).

The eigenvalues of π^m are the a_i^m, and weights relative to q^m of the a_i^m equal weights relative to q of the a_i (EDC.7/weight-weil-number-base-extension, EDC.7/weight-finite-field-base-extension-of-weights).
𝒢₀ corresponds to a representation of π₁(U₀, u) trivial on π₁(U, u), so it factors through π₁(U₀)/π₁(U) = Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q).
The Frobenius at x maps to F^{deg x} in Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q), so its eigenvalues are the α_i^{deg x} (EDC.7/weight-finite-field-base-extension-of-weights).

hypotheses: Z(X_x, t) ∈ ℚ(t) is the rationality of the zeta function over ℚ: Z(X_x, t) ∈ ℤ[[t]] is rational over ℚ_ℓ by the cohomological formula, so DWP.0/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou (a) applies. The cohomological formula is Weil I (1.5.4), requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2.
Common α_i = β_j can be cancelled, so they may be assumed distinct. This is the finite eigenvalue family bookkeeping RS-17 asks for, with no appeal to purity.
No Riemann hypothesis is used: the α and β are arbitrary ℓ-adic units.
proofSteps: For x ∈ |U₀|, the fibre X_x is smooth projective over k(x), and H^i(X_x̄) is the stalk of R^i f_*ℚ_ℓ at a geometric point over x (proper base change, SF.2).
Filter R^n by ℰ ∩ ℰ^⊥ ⊆ ℰ ⊆ R^n: the factor splits as det(on R^n/ℰ)·det(on ℰ ∩ ℰ^⊥)·det(on ℱ₀) (EDC.7/weight-endomorphism-weights).
Lemma geometrically-constant-lisse-sheaves on R^i (i ≠ n), R^n/ℰ₀ and ℰ₀ ∩ ℰ₀^⊥ gives the α and β factors. Cancel common values.
Z(X_x, t) ∈ ℚ(t), by the cohomological formula and DWP.0/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou (a).

hypotheses: The atlas's completion contract for DWP.3 splits this into two steps. The first is finite-quotient Chebotarev with constant-field degree congruences (DWP.3/function-field-chebotarev, applied to the finite quotients of the ℓ-adic image). The second is the approximation of the closed Haar-null set by open neighbourhoods of small measure, proved here. Topological density alone does not give density zero.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.4/smooth-pro.statement: For every smooth projective X₀ over 𝔽_q and every i≥0, each eigenvalue of geometric Frobenius on Hⁱ(X,ℚ_ℓ) is a Weil q-number of weight i. This is Weil I Lemma 1.7; integral cohomological factors and their ℓ-independence (Weil I Theorem 1.6) are DWP.4/integral-cohomological-factors.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.10/compatibl.statement: For smooth projective X₀/𝔽_q, the integral factors Π_i of DWP.4/integral-cohomological-factors identify the Weil weight-i root multisets across every ℓ≠p, and DWP.10/point-count-bounds gives the all-extension point-count estimate. The endpoint for a pure-dimensional scheme with geometric-component permutation σ is c_n(1+q^(nd)), with c_n=#Fix(σⁿ), rather than a universal single q^(nd). To export a compatible stable arithmetic subquotient, supply a normalized rational factor Q(T), independent of ℓ, whose image is exactly its Frobenius factor in every realization. Under that additional hypothesis its roots and weights agree across realizations; purity of the ambient space alone does not construct Q.
proofSteps: Use the canonical degree-factor theorem DWP.4/integral-cohomological-factors (through DWP.0/weight-separated-factor-extraction) and the component-aware bound DWP.10/point-count-bounds. Use smooth-projective purity only as their weight input, not as a second proof of those owners’ targets.

For a supplied rational subquotient factor use the coefficient embeddings and the ambient purity theorem to transfer the common root multiset. Factor identification is an input; no arbitrary Hecke constituent is declared compatible.
Track geometric component permutation under each extension, and treat dimension zero by its exact finite-étale cycle formula.

sources.match: Degree factors and the smooth-projective Weil conclusions, planned here as DWP.4/integral-cohomological-factors and DWP.10/point-count-bounds.
Independence of the smooth proper degree factors; compatible subquotient factors still require their own rational factor input.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.10/frobenius.statement: In Weil II §2.2’s algebraic-by-ℤ monodromy setting, let X₀/𝔽_q be normal and geometrically connected of dimension N≥1, with the hypotheses (a)–(c) and compact form G_R of EDC.7/weight-compact-weil-form (finite kernel is required on the geometric subgroup). Let G_R^i denote degree-i conjugacy classes with the pushforward of normalized compact Haar. For a central z of positive degree d and fixed i, translate by z^(−n) the measure q^(−(nd+i)N) Σ_(x∈X₀(𝔽_(q^(nd+i)))) δ_[ιF_x,ss]. As n→∞ it converges weakly to Haar on the degree-i conjugacy fibre. The sum is over rational points with Frobenius powers, and normalization uses the base dimension N. This is Weil II (3.5.3), not Weil I’s estimate or density of individual Weil numbers.
proofSteps: For every irreducible continuous unitary representation of G_R, the corresponding algebraic representation gives a coefficient sheaf ι-pure of weight zero by the compact-form equivalence. Import the general compact-support bounds of Weil II (3.3.4) through DWP.7/cohomological-bounds-3-3-2-3-3-6, with the real-ι variant EDC.7/weight-iota-mixed-direct-image-3-3-10, to continue its Euler product, with no zero or pole to the right of N−1/2 except the simple trivial norm-character pole at N. Normality/geometric connectedness identify the top-degree invariant contribution. Nonunitary central weights must be normalized before this analytic boundary is used.
Rescale the norm character to replace the abstract convergence boundary 1 by N and apply the degree-fibre equidistribution theorem.

Use (3.5.2.1): a degree-e closed point contributes e rational points when e divides m, each with local Frobenius F_x^(m/e). This identifies prime-power degree measures with the rational-point measure. Retain the central translation and every residue class i modulo d.
Import explicit ℙᴺ/𝔾_m cohomology from EDC.3 rather than proving it again. Check each Tate sign against geometric Frobenius q⁻¹ on ℚ_ℓ(1).
Use initial curve purity and the alternating duality pairing for Yu’s σ_iσ_(i+g)=q bookkeeping, including multiplicity and odd/zero genus cases.

For the supplied pure Rankin–Selberg coefficient, use sharp proper curve purity and numeric disjoint-weight spectra. Import its Euler determinant formula from SF.2 and its duality from EDC.2; this proves only the weight input to Yu §6.1.1.
Import semistable weights and the component formula of DWP.10/point-count-bounds; retain the strict difference between purity of projective cohomology and mixed compact-support cohomology.
Define the stalkwise predicate on Frobenius modules first, through the eigenvalue multiset of EDC.7/weight-endomorphism-weights, and the sheaf predicate as its conjunction over |X|.

Stability under subsheaves, quotients and extensions: the eigenvalue multiset of an extension is the union of those of sub and quotient (EDC.7/weight-endomorphism-weights via EDC.7/weight-purity-under-subquotients-and-extensions).

Pullback along g : Y → X: for y ∈ |Y| over x, F_y acts on (g*ℱ)_ȳ = ℱ_x̄ as F_x^{[k(y):k(x)]}; powers of algebraic integers are algebraic integers. Finite direct image: the stalk of f_*ℱ at y is the sum of the induced modules of the stalks at the points over y, whose Frobenius eigenvalues are roots of the eigenvalues at those points (EDC.7/weight-spectra-of-polynomials-in-an-endomorphism), and roots of algebraic integers are algebraic integers.
Tensor products: eigenvalues multiply (EDC.7/weight-spectra-of-tensor-products-and-duals). Twist ℱ(−m), m ≥ 0: eigenvalues multiply by N(x)^m.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralEnd
api.statement: IsIntegralEnd (F : V →ₗ[E] V) : Prop := ∀ α ∈ eigenvalues F, IsIntegral ℤ α, for E a field of characteristic 0 and V finite-dimensional, with eigenvalues F the multiset of roots (EDC.7/weight-endomorphism-weights) of the characteristic polynomial in an algebraic closure.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralSheaf
api.statement: IsIntegralSheaf ℱ : Prop := ∀ x ∈ |X|, IsIntegralEnd (F_x acting on ℱ_x̄).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.isIntegralEnd_iff_charpoly
api.statement: IsIntegralEnd F ↔ every root of det(T − F) in an algebraic closure is integral over ℤ; when det(T − F) has rational coefficients this holds iff it has integer coefficients.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralEnd.of_extension
api.statement: For an F-stable subspace W ⊆ V: IsIntegralEnd F ↔ IsIntegralEnd (F|W) ∧ IsIntegralEnd (F on V/W).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralEnd.pow
api.statement: IsIntegralEnd F → IsIntegralEnd (F ^ r) for r ≥ 1, and conversely: an algebraic number with an integral power is integral.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralEnd.tensor
api.statement: IsIntegralEnd F → IsIntegralEnd G → IsIntegralEnd (F ⊗ G).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralSheaf.comap
api.statement: Pullback along any morphism of schemes of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] preserves integrality.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralSheaf.finite_pushforward
api.statement: Direct image along a finite morphism preserves integrality.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralSheaf.twist_neg
api.statement: ℱ integral and m ≥ 0 ⇒ ℱ(−m) integral; the converse fails for m > 0.

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralSheaf.weights_nonneg
api.statement: An integral mixed sheaf has all punctual weights ≥ 0 (Weil II 3.3.2): the norm of an integral Weil q-number of weight n and degree d is a nonzero integer of absolute value q^{nd/2} (EDC.7/weight-weil-number-arithmetic (iv)).

api.name: TauCeti.Weights.IsIntegralSheaf.constant
api.statement: The constant sheaf ℚ̄_ℓ is integral; so is every sheaf ℱ whose Frobenius traces at all closed points of all finite extensions are algebraic integers.

proofSteps: Upper bound: EDC.7/weight-fundamental-direct-image-theorem-3-3-1.
Lower bound 0: R^i f_!ℱ is integral (DWP.7/deligne-integrality-theorem-sga7-xxi) and mixed, so its weights are ≥ 0 (api IsIntegralSheaf.weights_nonneg).
Lower bound 2(i − d) for i > d: R^i f_!ℱ(i − d) is integral and mixed with weights shifted by −2(i − d), hence ≥ 0.
(i) is the case Y = Spec 𝔽_q of EDC.7/weight-fundamental-direct-image-theorem-3-3-1 and DWP.7/integral-weight-bounds-3-3-3.

(ii) Reduce to X₀ of pure dimension N (components). The dual ℱ₀^∨ is lisse and mixed of weights ≤ −n. By (i), H^{2N−i}_c(X, ℱ^∨)(N) is mixed of weights ≤ −n + (2N − i) − 2N = −n − i (reading ℱ^∨ in the printed proof, PAPER-DELIGNE-80/E45). Poincaré duality (EDC.2) gives a Frobenius-equivariant perfect pairing H^i(X, ℱ) × H^{2N−i}_c(X, ℱ^∨)(N) → ℚ̄_ℓ, so the eigenvalues on H^i(X, ℱ) are the inverses of those on H^{2N−i}_c(X, ℱ^∨)(N) (EDC.7/weight-reciprocal-pairing-of-eigenvalues) and have weights ≥ n + i.
(iii) The image is a quotient of H^i_c (weights ≤ n + i by (i)) and a subspace of H^i (weights ≥ n + i by (ii)), hence pure of weight n + i (EDC.7/weight-purity-under-subquotients-and-extensions).
(iv) Use EDC.7/weight-iota-mixed-direct-image-3-3-10 in place of 3.3.1; the duality step is unchanged.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7/newton-cou.statement: Let q = p^f, n ∈ ℤ, and α an algebraic number which is a Weil q-number of weight n (EDC.7/weight-weil-q-number). Let K be a number field containing α and v a valuation of K above p, normalised by v(q) = 1, extended to v : K → ℚ ∪ {∞}. The couple of α at v is (r, s) = (v(α), v(q^n α⁻¹)). Here q^n α⁻¹ ∈ K, and under every embedding σ : K → ℂ it maps to the complex conjugate of σ(α) (EDC.7/weight-weil-number-arithmetic (iii)); so q^n α⁻¹ has the same minimal polynomial over ℚ as α, i.e. it is a Galois conjugate of α. Always r + s = n; if α is integral over ℤ then r ≥ 0 and s ≥ 0.

hypotheses: (i), (ii): X₀ proper AND smooth; projectivity is not assumed
(iii): the exact dualizing-object hypothesis Ra^!ℚ_ℓ ≅ ℚ_ℓ(N)[2N], not a weaker 'rationally smooth' slogan; coefficients constant
(ii)'s integrality and ℓ-independence use the algebraic factor lemma DWP.0/weight-separated-factor-extraction

Source convention Weil II (0.1): schemes in this node are separated noetherian schemes with ℓ invertible. The packet uses the scheme specialisation explicitly permitted there, rather than claiming the algebraic-space generalisation.
proofSteps: (i) For X₀ proper, H^i_c = H^i, so DWP.7/cohomological-bounds-3-3-2-3-3-6 (iii) gives purity of weight n + i; the ι-version uses (iv) of that node.

(ii) Purity of weight i is (i) with ℱ₀ = ℚ_ℓ (n = 0). The zeta function Z(X₀, t) = ∏_i det(1 − F t, H^i)^{(−1)^{i+1}} is in ℚ(t) with integral power-series expansion and does not depend on ℓ (trace formula, SF.2). Since the factors of different degrees have reciprocal roots of different absolute values, no cancellation occurs, and the algebraic factor lemma DWP.0/weight-separated-factor-extraction (the argument of Weil I, proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6)), after DWP.0/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou puts Z(X₀, t) in ℚ(t), extracts each det(1 − F t, H^i) as a polynomial with integer coefficients determined by Z(X₀, t), hence independent of ℓ.

(iii) In the proofs of DWP.7/cohomological-bounds-3-3-2-3-3-6 (ii)–(iii) and of (i), smoothness enters only through Poincaré duality H^i(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) ≅ H^{2N−i}_c(X, ℚ̄_ℓ(N))^∨, which follows from Ra^!ℚ_ℓ ≅ ℚ_ℓ(N)[2N] and Verdier duality RΓ(X, Ra^!ℚ_ℓ) = RHom(RΓ_c(X, ℚ_ℓ), ℚ_ℓ) (EDC.1).

For π : Y → Y/G with Y smooth of dimension N, the constant sheaf on Y/G is the G-invariant summand of π_*ℚ_ℓ: geometric fibres are single G-orbits, and the averaging idempotent |G|⁻¹∑g exists in ℚ_ℓ even if p divides |G|. Finite proper pushforward commutes with Verdier duality (EDC.1). The self-duality D(π_*ℚ_ℓ) ≅ π_*ℚ_ℓ(N)[2N] from EDC.2 intertwines g with g⁻¹, so the averaging idempotent is self-adjoint. Its image therefore inherits Dℚ_ℓ ≅ ℚ_ℓ(N)[2N]. Glue étale-locally to obtain the rational-homology-manifold condition.

Independence of the filtration in (b): two such filtrations have a common refinement (Schreier/Zassenhaus) whose graded pieces are subquotients of both, and mixedness is stable under subquotients and extensions (EDC.7/weight-punctual-purity-and-mixedness).

Independence of the finite extension in (c): mixedness of a sheaf on X_s is unchanged by the finite base extension k(s) ⊂ k(s′) (Frobenius powers, EDC.7/weight-finite-field-base-extension-of-weights), and any two finite extensions are dominated by a third.
Quasi-unipotence (SGA 7 I, LPV.1) guarantees that (c) is always applicable.
By the monodromy theorem (LPV.1) replace the trait by a finite extension so that I acts unipotently, through its quotient ℤ_ℓ(1).

The monodromy filtration constructions of Weil II (1.6.1), (1.6.14) (LPV.1 for the linear algebra, EDC.7/weight-local-weight-corollaries for its weight interpretation) reduce mixedness of R^iΨ(ℱ) to mixedness of the inertia invariants (R^iΨ(ℱ))^I.

As in the proof of Weil II (3.6.1), these invariants are quotients of u*R^iv_*(ℱ|X_η), where u : X_s → X and v : X_η → X are the inclusions (specialisation sequence of LPV.0); they are mixed by EDC.7/weight-six-operations-preserve-mixedness-6-1-11.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/intermedia.statement: (c) Let X₀ be a smooth curve over 𝔽_q, j : U₀ → X₀ a dense open and ℱ₀ a lisse sheaf on U₀, punctually pure of weight w (equivalently, by EDC.7/weight-twist-shift-and-smooth-lisse-purity-6-2-5, ℱ₀ is pure of weight w as a sheaf). Then j_*ℱ₀ is pure of weight w. (d) Let X₀ be smooth, D₀ ⊂ X₀ a smooth divisor, j : U₀ = X₀ − D₀ → X₀, and ℱ₀ lisse on U₀, punctually pure of weight w and tamely ramified along D₀. Then j_*ℱ₀ is pure of weight w. The ι-variants hold.
proofSteps: Upper bound: j_*ℱ₀ is mixed (Weil II (1.8.9), EDC.7/weight-local-weight-corollaries) and its stalks at points of D₀ (or of X₀ − U₀) are the inertia invariants of ℱ, contained in Ker N ⊂ M₀ (Weil II (1.8.8) 1) and 2)), of weights ≤ w (EDC.7's local weight theorem, EDC.7/weight-local-monodromy-purity). So j_*ℱ₀ has weights ≤ w.

Lower bound: D(j_*ℱ₀) = j_*(Dℱ₀) up to the shift and twist of the smooth dualizing complex, by the formula RHom(j_*ℱ, ℚ̄_ℓ) = j_*ℋom(ℱ, ℚ̄_ℓ) (Weil II's argument; local duality on a smooth curve or along a smooth divisor for tame ℱ, EDC.1–EDC.2). Since ℱ₀^∨ is lisse and punctually pure of weight −w, the first step gives weights ≤ −w for D(j_*ℱ₀) after renormalising by EDC.7/weight-twist-shift-and-smooth-lisse-purity-6-2-5 (a).

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/variant-ov.statement: For X of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ] with structure map a : X → Spec ℤ[1/ℓ], put K′_X = Ra^!ℚ̄_ℓ and D′ = RHom(−, K′_X). Call K ∈ D^b_c(X) pure of weight w when K is mixed of weights ≤ w (EDC.7/weight-mixed-complexes, read on schemes of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ]) and D′K is mixed of weights ≤ −w. If X is of finite type over 𝔽_p then K′_X = K_X(−1)[−2], so D′ = D(−1)[−2] and this notion agrees with that of EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes. Proper direct images preserve this purity: for f : X → Y proper over ℤ[1/ℓ] and K pure of weight w, Rf_*K is pure of weight w.
proofSteps: For i : Spec 𝔽_p → Spec ℤ[1/ℓ], i^!ℚ̄_ℓ = ℚ̄_ℓ(−1)[−2]: this is the local cohomology of the henselisation of ℤ_(p), a discrete valuation ring with ℓ invertible, computed by Kummer theory (requested from EDC.1, which identifies i_*i^! with local cohomology; it is the dimension-one case, not Gabber's general absolute purity). So K′_X = Ra_p^! i^!ℚ̄_ℓ = K_X(−1)[−2] and D′K = DK(−1)[−2]; by EDC.7/weight-twist-shift-and-smooth-lisse-purity-6-2-5 (a) with N = −1 the two bounds agree.

Rf_! preserves weights ≤ w over ℤ[1/ℓ] by EDC.7/weight-fundamental-direct-image-theorem-3-3-1 and the spectral sequence of EDC.7/weight-compact-support-direct-image-upper-weights-6-2-3; for f proper D′Rf_* = Rf_*D′ (EDC.1 over ℤ[1/ℓ]); conclude as in EDC.7/weight-proper-direct-image-preserves-purity-6-2-6.
ℋom(ℱ, 𝒢) is lisse and punctually ι-pure of weight γ − β (EDC.7/weight-spectra-of-tensor-products-and-duals).

By DWP.7/cohomological-bounds-3-3-2-3-3-6 (ii) in its ι-form (iv), H¹(X, ℋom(ℱ, 𝒢)) has ι-weights ≥ γ − β + 1, and by EDC.7/weight-iota-mixed-direct-image-3-3-10 they lie in γ − β + ℤ. F has a nonzero invariant only if it has eigenvalue 1, of weight 0; so H¹(X, ℋom)^F ≠ 0 forces 0 ∈ (γ − β + ℤ) and 0 ≥ γ − β + 1, i.e. β ≡ γ mod ℤ and β > γ. By DWP.8/ext-one-of-lisse-sheaves-3-4-2 a geometrically nontrivial extension has nonzero image in H¹(X, ℋom)^F.

(3.4.4) The H⁰ term H⁰(X, ℋom(ℱ, 𝒢)) ⊂ ℋom(ℱ, 𝒢)_x̄ has ι-weight γ − β; its F-coinvariants are nonzero only if F has eigenvalue 1, forcing γ = β. Combine with the previous step through the exact sequence.

(3.4.6) Uniqueness and functoriality: the stalk formula is forced, since a summand whose weights lie in b must contain the generalised eigenspaces of weights in b and no others (DWP.0/weight-decomposition (ii), DWP.0/disjoint-spectra-no-intertwiner).

(3.4.7) Existence for X₀ smooth and ℱ₀ a successive extension of lisse punctually ι-pure sheaves: induction on the length; if ℱ₀ is an extension of ℱ″₀ (decomposed) by ℱ′₀ pure of weight β with class b, then for b′ ≠ b the preimage of ℱ″₀(b′) is a trivial extension by DWP.8/extensions-between-pure-lisse-sheaves-3-4-3-3-4-4 (Ext¹ = 0 when the weights are not congruent mod ℤ); take ℱ₀(b) the preimage of ℱ″₀(b) and ℱ₀(b′) a lifting of ℱ″₀(b′).

(3.4.8) General case by induction on dim X₀: replacing X₀ by X₀,red, choose a dense open j : U₀ → X₀ where (3.4.7) applies (generic lissity and smoothness; Weil II (1.8.11), EDC.7/weight-local-weight-corollaries, on a normal U₀); the induction hypothesis applies on the complement i : F₀ → X₀. Glue through the equivalence ℱ₀ ↦ (j*ℱ₀, i*ℱ₀, specialisation s : i*ℱ₀ → i*j_*j*ℱ₀); s maps (i*ℱ₀)(b) into i*j_*((j*ℱ₀)(b)) because, by Weil II (1.8.9) (EDC.7/weight-local-weight-corollaries) and twisting, the punctual weights of i*j_*((j*ℱ₀)(b)) lie in b.
Twist: if c has ι-weight β₀ ∈ b, then ℱ₀(b)^{(c⁻¹)} has integer ι-weights (Weil II 1.2.7, EDC.7/weight-twisting-by-rank-one-characters).

(3.4.6) Uniqueness and functoriality: the stalk formula is forced (DWP.0/weight-decomposition (ii)); a morphism preserves generalised eigenspaces, so f(W_i) ⊆ W_i, and strictness f(W_iℱ₀) = f(ℱ₀) ∩ W_i𝒢₀ holds stalkwise because both sides are the sum of the generalised eigenspaces of weight ≤ i of f(ℱ_x̄).

(3.4.7) Existence for X₀ smooth and ℱ₀ a successive extension of lisse punctually ι-pure sheaves: if ℱ₀ is an extension of ℱ″₀ (filtered) by ℱ′₀ pure of integer weight β, then the preimage of W_{β−1}ℱ″₀ is a trivial extension of W_{β−1}ℱ″₀ by ℱ′₀ (DWP.8/extensions-between-pure-lisse-sheaves-3-4-3-3-4-4: Ext¹(pure of weight < β, pure of weight β) = 0); for i < β take W_iℱ₀ a lifting of W_iℱ″₀, for i ≥ β the preimage of W_iℱ″₀.

(3.4.8) General X₀: uniqueness allows descent, so assume X₀ normal; then ℱ₀ = j_*j*ℱ₀ for a dense open j : U₀ → X₀ where (3.4.7) applies (Weil II (1.8.11), EDC.7/weight-local-weight-corollaries), and W_iℱ₀ := j_*W_ij*ℱ₀ gives Gr^W_i ℱ₀ = j_*Gr^W_i j*ℱ₀, which is lisse and punctually ι-pure of weight i by Weil II (1.8.10) (EDC.7/weight-local-weight-corollaries).
Independence of ι for mixed sheaves: the eigenvalues are Weil numbers whose weight does not depend on ι (EDC.7/weight-weil-number-iff-iota-pure-for-every-iota), so the stalk formula does not either.

(3.4.5) For U₀ ⊂ X₀ a dense open and ū a geometric point of U₀, π₁(U, ū) → π₁(X, ū) is surjective (X normal, IG.0); so geometric semisimplicity may be checked on U₀ (EDC.7/weight-geometric-semisimplicity, api isGeometricallySemisimple_iff_restrict_open), and one may assume X₀ smooth.

Let ℱ′ be the largest semisimple lisse subsheaf of ℱ (sum of its irreducible lisse subsheaves). It is Frobenius-stable by transport of structure, hence comes from ℱ′₀ ⊂ ℱ₀; put ℱ″₀ = ℱ₀/ℱ′₀. Both are punctually ι-pure of weight β.

By DWP.8/extensions-between-pure-lisse-sheaves-3-4-3-3-4-4 (equal weights, so β > γ fails), the extension of ℱ″₀ by ℱ′₀ is geometrically trivial. If ℱ″ ≠ 0, a simple lisse subsheaf of ℱ″ lifts to ℱ through the geometric splitting, contradicting the maximality of ℱ′. Hence ℱ″ = 0 and ℱ = ℱ′ is semisimple.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.8/potentiall.statement: Let k be algebraically closed with ℓ invertible, X a normal scheme of finite type over k, and ℱ a lisse sheaf on X which is potentially punctually ι-pure (EDC.7/weight-potentially-property-p-3-4-10). Then ℱ is semisimple.
proofSteps: Choose a model (S, x̄, X_S, ℱ_S) and shrink S so that X_S → S has normal geometric fibres and ℱ_S is lisse (generic normality and lissity, L2).

By the specialisation theorem for monodromy groups (Weil II (1.11.1) with (1.11.5), EDC.7/weight-specialization-of-monodromy), after shrinking S the image of π₁ of the geometric generic fibre in GL(ℱ_x̄) is conjugate to the image of π₁ of the geometric fibre X_s̄ at closed points s, i.e. the geometric monodromy groups of ℱ and of ℱ_S|X_s̄ agree.

ℱ_S|X_s is lisse and punctually ι-pure on the normal X_s over the finite field k(s), so it is geometrically semisimple by DWP.8/geometric-semisimplicity-theorem-3-4-1-iii; semisimplicity is a property of the monodromy group, so ℱ is semisimple.

Exactness of 0 → j_!ℚ_ℓ → ℚ_ℓ → ν_{1*}ε_1 → ν_{2*}ε_2 → ⋯ → ν_{d*}ε_d → 0 on X₀: étale locally D₀ is a union of coordinate hyperplanes and the complex is the augmented Čech (Mayer–Vietoris) resolution of the extension by zero, with the signs organised by the orientation sheaves (EDC.0, SF.2).

Applying RΓ(X, −) and filtering by the stupid filtration gives E₁^{m,k} = H^k(X, ν_{m*}ε_m) = H^k(D^{(m)}, ε_m) ⇒ H^{m+k}(X, j_!ℚ_ℓ) = H^{m+k}_c(U); the differential d₁ is induced by the maps of the resolution, the signed restriction maps.

Each D^{(m)}₀ is smooth proper of dimension d − m and ε_m is a lisse sheaf of finite order, punctually pure of weight 0, so E₁^{m,k} is pure of weight k (DWP.7/hodge-type-triangles-and-proper-smooth-purity-3-3-7-3-3-11 (i); for stacks, DWP.7/purity-of-smooth-proper-dm-stacks).

d_r : E_r^{m,k} → E_r^{m+r,k−r+1} is a Frobenius-equivariant map between pure modules of weights k and k − r + 1, hence zero for r ≥ 2 (DWP.0/disjoint-spectra-no-intertwiner); so E₂ = E_∞ and the abutment filtration has pure graded pieces E₂^{m,k} of weight k, which identifies it with the weight filtration (DWP.0/weight-decomposition).

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9/arithmetic.statement: Let k be algebraically closed with ℓ invertible in k, X a smooth projective k-scheme of pure dimension n and L a very ample line bundle, with X ⊂ P = ℙ^N_k the embedding it defines. There are an integral scheme S of finite type over ℤ[1/ℓ], a morphism x̄ : Spec k → S, a smooth projective morphism f_S : X_S → S of pure relative dimension n with a closed embedding X_S ⊂ ℙ^N_S (L_S = 𝒪(1)|X_S), and an isomorphism (X_S ⊂ ℙ^N_S) ×_S k ≅ (X ⊂ P). For such a model: (i) R^jf_{S*}ℚ_ℓ is lisse and its formation commutes with base change; for every geometric point s̄ of S the cospecialisation isomorphisms H^*(X_s̄, ℚ_ℓ) ≅ H^*(X, ℚ_ℓ) are ring isomorphisms compatible with the traces and carry c₁(L_s̄) to c₁(L); in particular hard Lefschetz holds for (X, L) iff it holds for (X_s̄, L_s̄) for one (equivalently every) closed point s of S. (ii) ℚ̄_ℓ[0] on X is potentially pure of weight 0, with this model (EDC.7/weight-potentially-property-p-3-4-10). (iii) If U_S ⊂ ℙ̌^N_S is the open subscheme of hyperplanes whose section of X_S is smooth over S and g_S : Z_S → U_S the family of these sections, then g_S is smooth projective, its fibre over k is the family g : Z → U of smooth hyperplane sections of X, and R^jg_*ℚ_ℓ is potentially punctually pure of weight j.
proofSteps: Noetherian approximation (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L2): write k as the filtered union of its finitely generated ℤ[1/ℓ]-subalgebras A; X ⊂ ℙ^N_k is defined by finitely many equations, so descends to X_A ⊂ ℙ^N_A for some A; smoothness, properness, flatness and pure relative dimension n descend after enlarging A and inverting an element. Take S = Spec A.

(i) Proper and smooth base change (SF.2): R^jf_{S*}ℚ_ℓ is lisse and commutes with base change; S is connected, so the stalks at any two geometric points are identified along étale paths. Cup product R^a ⊗ R^b → R^{a+b}, the relative trace R^{2n}f_{S*}ℚ_ℓ(n) → ℚ_ℓ (EDC.2) and c₁(L_S) ∈ H⁰(S, R²f_{S*}ℚ_ℓ(1)) (EDC.3, compatible with base change) are morphisms or sections of lisse sheaves, so the identifications respect them.
(ii) On each closed fibre X_s, smooth over the finite field k(s), ℚ̄_ℓ[0] is pure of weight 0 (EDC.7/weight-twist-shift-and-smooth-lisse-purity-6-2-5 (b)).

(iii) The incidence family is smooth over the open of hyperplanes giving smooth sections (LPV.3/dual-variety, which is the fibre over k; openness over S by the Jacobian criterion), and DWP.8/proper-smooth-direct-images-are-potentially-pure-3-4-11 applies to g_S over each closed point of S.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9/lefschetz-.statement: Parts (i) and (ii) are EDC.7/abstract-primitive-decomposition, for the graded Lefschetz object (EDC.7/graded-lefschetz-object) in finite-dimensional K-vector spaces with the trivial twist, after reindexing V^{n+j} as L^j; they are cited here, not planned again. This node owns (iii), the Lefschetz pairings on the primitive parts. Let K be a field, n ∈ ℕ, V a finite-dimensional K-vector space which is the internal direct sum of subspaces V^j (0 ≤ j ≤ 2n; V^j = 0 otherwise), and λ ∈ End(V) with λ(V^j) ⊆ V^{j+2}, such that λ^r : V^{n−r} → V^{n+r} is bijective for 0 ≤ r ≤ n. Put P^{n−r} = V^{n−r} ∩ ker λ^{r+1} for 0 ≤ r ≤ n. Then: (i) for 0 ≤ r ≤ n, the maps ⊕_{k ≥ 0} λ^k : ⊕_{k≥0} P^{n−r−2k} → V^{n−r} and ⊕_{k ≥ 0} λ^{r+k} : ⊕_{k≥0} P^{n−r−2k} → V^{n+r} are isomorphisms; (ii) dim P^{n−r} = dim V^{n−r} − dim V^{n−r−2}; (iii) if B is a nondegenerate bilinear form on V with B(V^a, V^b) = 0 unless a + b = 2n and B(λx, y) = B(x, λy), then for 0 ≤ r ≤ n the form ψ_r(x, y) = B(λ^r x, y) on V^{n−r} is nondegenerate, the decomposition (i) of V^{n−r} is ψ_r-orthogonal, and ψ_r restricts to a nondegenerate form on P^{n−r}; if moreover B(y, x) = (−1)^a B(x, y) for x ∈ V^a, then ψ_r is (−1)^{n−r}-symmetric.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9/hard-lefsc.statement: Let k be algebraically closed with ℓ invertible, X ⊂ P = ℙ^N_k a projective k-scheme, η = c₁(𝒪_X(1)) ∈ H²(X, ℚ_ℓ(1)), and K ∈ D^b_c(X, ℚ̄_ℓ) a potentially pure complex, with a model (S, x̄, X_S ⊂ ℙ^N_S, K_S) witnessing potential purity (EDC.7/weight-potentially-property-p-3-4-10). Let n ∈ ℤ be such that for every i, dim Supp ℋ^i(K) ≤ n − i and dim Supp ℋ^i(DK[−2n]) ≤ n − i (dim ∅ = −∞), where D is duality relative to k. Then for every r ≥ 0 the cup product η^r ∪ − : H^{n−r}(X, K) → H^{n+r}(X, K(r)) is an isomorphism.
proofSteps: Induction on dim X (Weil II 6.2.13, parallel to 4.1.1). If dim X = 0 and ℋ^iK ≠ 0, the hypotheses give 0 ≤ n − i and 0 ≤ n − (−i + 2n) = i − n, so i = n: H^iK = 0 for i ≠ n and the assertion is trivial.

For Y = X ∩ H_u a sufficiently general hyperplane section (u in the dense open U where the R^jg_*q*K are lisse), K|Y satisfies the hypotheses with n − 1, and D(K|Y) = (DK)|Y(−1)[−2] (generic transversality; LPV.7:invariant-cycles' proof of 6.2.11, SGA 4½ [Th. finitude] generic acyclicity through EDC.0). As in DWP.9/hyperplane-factorisation-4-1-2, using LPV.7's support-bound weak Lefschetz theorem 6.2.11 (i) for K and for DK, the induction reduces to r = 1, i.e. to the bijectivity of H^{n−1}(X, K) → H^{n−1}(Y, K) → H^{n+1}(X, K)(1), the second map being the transpose of restriction H^{n−1}(X, DK[−2n]) → H^{n−1}(Y, DK[−2n]).

It therefore suffices that the perfect duality (EDC.1, Verdier duality on the projective Y over the algebraically closed k) between H^{n−1}(Y, K) and H^{n−1}(Y, DK[−2n]) induces a perfect duality between the images of H^{n−1}(X, K) and H^{n−1}(X, DK[−2n]). By LPV.7's global invariant cycle theorem 6.2.12, applied to K and to DK[−2n] (both potentially pure, D preserving purity, EDC.7/weight-pure-complexes), these images are the π₁(U, u)-invariants. With twists restored, the pairing has values in ℚ̄_ℓ(1): on Y, D_Y(K|Y) = (DK)|Y(−1)[−2], so DK[−2n]|Y = D_Y(K|Y)(1)[−2(n−1)]. Over algebraically closed k this is a one-dimensional constant target; retain its twist when forming Gysin.

The representation of π₁(U, u) on H^*(Y_u, K) is semisimple: R^jg_*(q*K)|U is lisse and potentially punctually ι-pure (proper direct image preserves purity on the model, EDC.7/weight-proper-direct-image-preserves-purity-6-2-6 and DWP.8/variant-over-z-one-over-ell-6-2-7, and lisse cohomology sheaves of a pure complex on a smooth base are punctually pure, EDC.7/weight-twist-shift-and-smooth-lisse-purity-6-2-5), hence semisimple by DWP.8/potentially-pure-lisse-sheaves-are-semisimple-3-4-12. Conclude by DWP.9/invariant-form-on-invariants-4-1-4. More explicitly put A=H^{n−1}(Y,K) and B=H^{n−1}(Y,DK[−2n]). The incidence pullback is smooth, so it preserves purity up to the normalised duality twist/shift (EDC.7/weight-directional-weight-estimates); B is dual to A up to the constant Tate line. Thus A⊕B is semisimple with the nondegenerate hyperbolic pairing between A and B. Apply 4.1.4 to A⊕B, whose invariants are A^G⊕B^G; its nondegeneracy says precisely that the pairing A^G×B^G is perfect.
The source identifies ℤ_ℓ with ℤ_ℓ(1) to view η in H²(X, ℤ_ℓ); with the twist restored the target is H^{n+r}(X, K(r)).
K = ℱ[0] is potentially pure of weight w as a complex: on the smooth closed fibres of a model, a lisse punctually pure sheaf is pure (EDC.7/weight-twist-shift-and-smooth-lisse-purity-6-2-5 (b)).

Support conditions with the integer n: ℋ⁰K = ℱ has support of dimension n ≤ n − 0; DK[−2n] = ℱ^∨(n)[0] (X smooth of pure dimension n) likewise. Apply DWP.9/hard-lefschetz-for-potentially-pure-complexes-6-2-13.
For ℱ = R^jh_*ℚ_ℓ, potential purity is DWP.8/proper-smooth-direct-images-are-potentially-pure-3-4-11.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.10/mixed-nea.statement: The arithmetic consumers use the already planned DWP.8 theorem that nearby-cycle cohomology sheaves of a mixed sheaf remain mixed, and its proper direct-image purity over ℤ[1/ℓ]. For an integral weight-w eigenvalue, DWP.7’s Newton couple (r,s) satisfies r+s=w and r,s≥0; its cohomological valuation triangles retain the separate compact-support/proper and smooth ordinary hypotheses. EDC.7 (EDC.7/weight-weil-q-number, EDC.7/weight-iota-weight) supplies the shared numeric Weil/ι-weight predicates to RD.6; RD.6 supplies its own F-isocrystal fibres and defines pointwise purity and mixedness there.

hypotheses: This is an upper bound for H¹_c, not purity. Sharp curve-coefficient purity is EDC.7/weight-sharp-curve-purity.

proofSteps: Choose the smooth projective compactification. Local monodromy bounds j_*ℱ at the boundary by β. The exact sequence H⁰(boundary)→H¹_c(U,ℱ)→H¹(C,j_*ℱ) gives the required degree-one upper bound.
On affine components H⁰_c=0; on proper components H⁰ is the invariant space of weight β. H²_c is the coinvariant space (−1), of weight β+2. Handle components and finite base extension explicitly.

The dévissage of general Rf_! (EDC.7/weight-fundamental-direct-image-theorem-3-3-1) does not use this node: it treats relative curves directly (EDC.7/weight-purity-of-the-relative-curve-case). Over Y = Spec 𝔽_q that theorem and its ι-variant already give the upper bound in every degree; this node records the absolute curve statement with the parabolic part made explicit.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.10/finite-fi.statement: Let X₀ be a normal, geometrically connected scheme of finite type over 𝔽_q of dimension N ≥ 1 (Weil II (3.5.1); for N = 1 a smooth geometrically connected curve), and E₀→X₀ an elliptic family with nonconstant j-invariant. Import the full SL₂ geometric monodromy theorem of Weil II (3.5.5) from its universal elliptic-family/modular-curve supplier. Then the normalized H¹ Frobenius classes lie in SU(2). Define θ_x∈[0,π] by eigenvalues q^(m/2)e^(±iθ_x) at x∈X₀(𝔽_(q^m)); #E_x(𝔽_(q^m))=1+q^m−2q^(m/2)cos θ_x. The measures q^(−mN) Σ_(x∈X₀(𝔽_(q^m))) δ_(θ_x) converge to (2/π)sin²θ dθ. The printed density and point-count sign in (3.5.6)–(3.5.7) are corrected as the confirmed source issues record.
proofSteps: Import elliptic-family full geometric monodromy, including the level structure, finite-index fundamental-group image, and prime-to-p level hypothesis. The determinant q^m and compact-form comparison identify SU(2)×ℤ with action (g,m)↦q^(m/2)g.
Apply Frobenius equidistribution with N = dim X₀ (q^(−m) normalisation only when N = 1). Push Haar forward to the conjugacy angle using the compact-group Weyl integration supplier.
Check mass and trace moments explicitly: ∫(2/π)sin²θ=1; the normalized trace a=2cosθ has mean 0 and second moment 1. The Hasse interval is a∈[−2,2].

nodes.title: Rational power series descend to ℚ and have integral normalised numerator and denominator (Fatou)
nodes.statement: (a) Descent of rationality. Let k ⊂ L be fields and f ∈ k[[t]]. If there are A, B ∈ L[t] with B(0) ≠ 0 and Bf = A in L[[t]], then there are such A, B in k[t]; that is, k[[t]] ∩ L(t) = k(t) inside L((t)). (b) Local Fatou. Let ℓ be a prime (ℓ = p allowed), f ∈ 1 + tℤ_ℓ[[t]], and G, H ∈ ℚ_ℓ[t] coprime with G(0) = H(0) = 1 and Hf = G. Then G, H ∈ ℤ_ℓ[t]. (c) Global Fatou. If f ∈ 1 + tℤ[[t]] lies in ℚ(t), there are unique coprime A, B ∈ 1 + tℤ[t] with f = A/B; the reciprocal roots of A and of B are algebraic integers. The equality is in ℚ[[t]], and A, B do not depend on any auxiliary field in which f was first shown to be rational.
hypotheses: (a): any field extension k ⊂ L.
(b): f has ℓ-adically integral coefficients and constant term 1; G, H coprime with constant term 1.
(c): f has integer coefficients and constant term 1.
proofSteps: (a) Bf = A with deg A ≤ N and deg B ≤ M is a system of linear equations over k in the coefficients of A and B; equivalently the Hankel determinants of order > M of the coefficient sequence of f beyond degree N vanish. A linear system with coefficients in k that has a nonzero solution over L has one over k, and B(0) ≠ 0 can be arranged after cancelling a power of t (Deligne, Weil I, proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), p. 276; Milne, Lemma 27.9).

(b) Work in a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ splitting H, with the extended absolute value. If a reciprocal root α of H had |α| > 1, then α⁻¹ lies in the open unit disc, where f converges because its coefficients have absolute value at most 1; evaluating Hf = G at α⁻¹ gives G(α⁻¹) = 0, contradicting coprimality. So the reciprocal roots of H have absolute value at most 1; since 1/f ∈ 1 + tℤ_ℓ[[t]] and (1/f)G = H, the same holds for G. Elementary symmetric functions of elements of absolute value at most 1 have absolute value at most 1 (Milne, Lemma 27.10, with the non-strict inequality at the boundary: Milne's proof prints a strict one, DeligneWeightsAndPurity/E10).

(c) Write f = A/B in lowest terms over ℚ with A(0) = B(0) = 1, which is possible because f(0) = 1 and B(0) ≠ 0 after (a). Apply (b) at every prime ℓ to get A, B ∈ ℤ_ℓ[t] for all ℓ, hence A, B ∈ ℤ[t]. The reciprocal roots of a polynomial in 1 + tℤ[t] are the roots of its reverse, a monic integer polynomial, hence algebraic integers (Deligne, Weil I, p. 276, Fatou's lemma).
acceptance: Z(ℙ¹_{𝔽_q}, t) = 1/((1 − t)(1 − qt)): A = 1 and B = (1 − t)(1 − qt) lie in 1 + tℤ[t].
Integrality cannot be dropped: f = 1/(1 − t/2) ∈ 1 + tℚ[[t]] is rational with denominator 1 − t/2 ∉ ℤ[t].
Coprimality cannot be dropped in (b): G = H = 1 − t/ℓ with f = 1 is a non-reduced presentation that is not integral.
Boundary case: f = 1/(1 − t) ∈ 1 + tℤ_ℓ[[t]] has a reciprocal root of absolute value exactly 1, so the bound in (b) is ≤ 1, not < 1.

uses.how: (a) puts the fibre zeta functions Z(X_x, t), integral and rational over ℚ_ℓ by the cohomological formula, into ℚ(t).
(c) gives the reduced integral presentation A/B that the pure factors are read off from.

sources.match: Shows by Hankel determinants that the integral zeta series, rational over ℚ_ℓ, is rational over ℚ, and invokes Fatou's lemma to give the coprime integral numerator and denominator constant term 1.

nodes.title: Weight separation: the pure factors of a rational zeta function are unique, rational and integral
nodes.statement: Let q > 1 be an integer and R ∈ 1 + tℤ[[t]] ∩ ℚ(t), written R = A/B with A, B ∈ 1 + tℤ[t] coprime (DWP.0/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou (c)). Let L be a field of characteristic 0 with algebraic closure L̄ and P_0, …, P_N ∈ 1 + tL[t] with ∏_{i=0}^{N} P_i^{(−1)^{i+1}} = R in L[[t]], such that every reciprocal root of P_i in L̄ is a Weil q-number of weight i (EDC.7/weight-weil-q-number). Then: (1) the P_i are pairwise coprime, and A = ∏_{i odd} P_i, B = ∏_{i even} P_i in L[t]; (2) for each i there is a unique Π_i ∈ 1 + tℤ[t] whose image in L[t] is P_i, namely Π_i = ∏(1 − αt)^{m(α)}, the product over the reciprocal roots α of A (i odd) or B (i even) that are Weil q-numbers of weight i, with their multiplicities m(α); (3) the reciprocal roots of Π_i are algebraic integers and deg Π_i = deg P_i; (4) if (P′_i) is a second family over another field L′ of characteristic 0 with the same R and the same purity property, then P_i and P′_i are images of the same Π_i. The integrality in (2)–(3) comes from Fatou's lemma and the separation of weights, not from the alternating product alone: without purity, cancellation between degrees can occur and R does not determine the factors.
hypotheses: q > 1 an integer; R ∈ 1 + tℤ[[t]] rational.
L a field of characteristic 0; P_i ∈ 1 + tL[t] with alternating product R.
Every reciprocal root of P_i is a Weil q-number of weight i (all complex conjugates of absolute value q^{i/2}).
proofSteps: Weights separate: a Weil q-number has a unique weight (EDC.7/weight-weil-q-number), so P_i and P_j have no common root for i ≠ j. Hence ∏_{i odd} P_i and ∏_{i even} P_i are coprime, and their quotient is a reduced presentation of R over L. Comparing with the reduced presentation A/B over ℚ, both normalised by constant term 1, gives (1).

Let K ⊂ L̄ be the splitting field over ℚ of AB. The set of reciprocal roots of AB of weight i, with multiplicities, is stable under Gal(K/ℚ), because being a Weil q-number of weight i depends only on the minimal polynomial over ℚ (EDC.7/weight-weil-q-number, EDC.7/weight-weil-number-arithmetic). So the coefficients of Π_i are fixed by Gal(K/ℚ) and lie in ℚ (mathlib:IsGalois.mem_range_algebraMap_iff_fixed).

The reverse of Π_i is a monic factor in ℚ[T] of the monic integral reverse of A or B, so by Gauss's lemma it has integer coefficients (mathlib:IsIntegrallyClosed.eq_map_mul_C_of_dvd); equivalently its roots are algebraic integers by DWP.0/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou (c).
Uniqueness and (4): Π_i is described by R alone, so any second pure family gives the same polynomials (Deligne, Weil I, end of the proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), p. 277).
acceptance: Elliptic curve E/𝔽_7, y² = x³ + x + 1, with #E(𝔽_7) = 5: R = (1 − 3t + 7t²)/((1 − t)(1 − 7t)) and Π_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t², whose reciprocal roots have absolute value 7^{1/2}.

Purity is needed: P_0 = 1, P_1 = P_2 = 1 − 2t give the alternating product R = 1, as do P_0 = P_1 = P_2 = 1, so R does not determine the factors; the hypothesis excludes this because 2 cannot be a Weil q-number of weight 1 and of weight 2.

nodes.title: Weil I, Theorem 1.6: integral, ℓ-independent factors of a smooth projective variety
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be a smooth projective variety over 𝔽_q, not assumed geometrically connected, X = X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q, and F the geometric Frobenius. For each i there is a unique Π_i ∈ 1 + tℤ[t] such that, for every prime ℓ ≠ p, the image of Π_i in ℚ_ℓ[t] is det(1 − tF | H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ)). Its degree is b_i = dim H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ), so the Betti numbers b_i do not depend on ℓ; its reciprocal roots are algebraic integers and Weil q-numbers of weight i; the Π_i are pairwise coprime; and Z(X₀, t) = ∏_i Π_i^{(−1)^{i+1}} is the reduced presentation of the zeta function, with numerator ∏_{i odd} Π_i and denominator ∏_{i even} Π_i. Frobenius semisimplicity is not part of the conclusion.
hypotheses: X₀ smooth and projective over 𝔽_q; geometric connectedness is not needed.
ℓ ≠ p; F is the geometric Frobenius, acting invertibly on each H^i.
The purity input is DWP.4/smooth-projective-purity, proved without Weil II; this is Weil I's route, before DWP.7.
proofSteps: The Euler product shows Z(X₀, t) ∈ 1 + tℤ[[t]], and the Grothendieck trace formula gives Z(X₀, t) = ∏_i det(1 − tF | H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ))^{(−1)^{i+1}} in ℚ_ℓ(t) (Weil I (1.5.4); SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2). So Z(X₀, t) lies in ℤ[[t]] ∩ ℚ_ℓ(t), hence in ℚ(t), with coprime A, B ∈ 1 + tℤ[t] (DWP.0/rational-zeta-descent-and-fatou (a), (c)).
Each P_i := det(1 − tF | H^i) has degree b_i because F is invertible, and its reciprocal roots are the eigenvalues of F, Weil q-numbers of weight i by DWP.4/smooth-projective-purity.

DWP.0/weight-separated-factor-extraction with L = ℚ_ℓ gives a unique Π_i ∈ 1 + tℤ[t] with image P_i, with algebraic integer reciprocal roots, and part (4) of that theorem shows Π_i is the same for every ℓ ≠ p. The reduced presentation is part (1).
acceptance: ℙⁿ: Π_{2i} = 1 − q^i t for 0 ≤ i ≤ n and Π_{2i+1} = 1.
Elliptic curve E/𝔽_7, y² = x³ + x + 1: Π_0 = 1 − t, Π_1 = 1 − 3t + 7t², Π_2 = 1 − 7t, and the trace formula gives #E(𝔽_7) = 1 + 7 − 3 = 5.
X₀ = ℙ¹_{𝔽_{q²}} regarded over 𝔽_q (two geometric components swapped by Frobenius): Π_0 = 1 − t², Π_2 = 1 − q²t², Π_1 = 1; the degrees are b_0 = b_2 = 2.
No complex fibre or characteristic-zero lift is used, and two primes ℓ, ℓ′ ≠ p give the same integer polynomial.

sources.match: Theorem 1.6 asserts that for a smooth projective variety over 𝔽_q the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius on each H^i has integer coefficients independent of ℓ and complex roots of absolute value q^{i/2}; the text deduces it from Lemma 1.7 by the rationality, Fatou and Galois-stability argument.

nodes.title: Point-count bounds for smooth projective varieties over 𝔽_q, with component permutations
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be a smooth projective variety over 𝔽_q of pure dimension d, X = X₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q, N_r = #X₀(𝔽_{q^r}), b_i = deg Π_i = dim H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ) (DWP.4/integral-cohomological-factors), and let σ be the permutation of the finite set π₀(X) of geometric connected components induced by Frobenius, c_r the number of components fixed by σ^r. (i) If d ≥ 1, then for every r ≥ 1, |N_r − c_r(1 + q^{dr})| ≤ Σ_{i=1}^{2d−1} b_i q^{ir/2}. (ii) If d = 0, X₀ is finite étale and N_r = c_r for every r ≥ 1; Z(X₀, t) = ∏_{cycles of σ} (1 − t^{length})⁻¹. (iii) In particular, for X₀ geometrically connected of dimension d ≥ 1, |N_r − (1 + q^{dr})| ≤ Σ_{i=1}^{2d−1} b_i q^{ir/2}, and for a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g, |N_r − (q^r + 1)| ≤ 2g q^{r/2}. The bound uses all interior degrees with their Betti numbers; it is not a statement about one degree.
hypotheses: X₀ smooth projective of pure dimension d over 𝔽_q; r ≥ 1.
The endpoint terms are traces on H⁰ and H^{2d}: for d = 0 only H⁰ occurs and both endpoints must not be subtracted.
proofSteps: Trace formula for proper X₀ (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2): N_r = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(F^r | H^i(X, ℚ_ℓ)), algebraic multiplicities and no diagonalisation.

H⁰(X, ℚ_ℓ) is the permutation representation of Frobenius on π₀(X), so Tr(F^r | H⁰) = c_r; for d ≥ 1, Poincaré duality identifies H^{2d} with the dual of H⁰ twisted by ℚ_ℓ(−d), so Tr(F^r | H^{2d}) = c_r q^{dr} (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2:pairings/extreme-degree-cohomology).

For 0 < i < 2d, Tr(F^r | H^i) is the sum of the r-th powers of the b_i eigenvalues, each of absolute value q^{i/2} under every complex embedding (DWP.4/smooth-projective-purity); the triangle inequality (mathlib:norm_sum_le) gives |Tr(F^r | H^i)| ≤ b_i q^{ir/2}. Sum over i.

d = 0: X₀ is a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite fields; a closed point of degree m has m points over 𝔽_{q^r} when m | r and none otherwise, which is c_r, and the Euler product gives the cycle formula.
acceptance: ℙ²: N_r = 1 + q^r + q^{2r}, the error is q^r and the bound b_2 q^r = q^r is attained.
A degree-two closed point Spec 𝔽_{q²}: N_r = 0, 2, 0, 2, … for r = 1, 2, 3, 4, and c_r is the same sequence.
Two projective lines exchanged by Frobenius (ℙ¹_{𝔽_{q²}} over 𝔽_q): c_r = 0 for odd r and 2 for even r, N_r = c_r(1 + q^r) exactly, as the bound with b_1 = 0 requires.
Genus-one curve E/𝔽_7, y² = x³ + x + 1: N_1 = 5 and |5 − 8| = 3 ≤ 2·7^{1/2}.

sources.match: (1.4)–(1.5) give the point count as the alternating sum of Frobenius traces; Theorem 8.1 proves the corresponding bound for a smooth complete intersection by combining that formula with the purity of Lemma 1.7, which is the argument stated here for all interior degrees.

nodes.title: Purity of the cohomology of smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stacks over 𝔽_q
nodes.statement: Let 𝒳₀ be a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack of finite type over 𝔽_q, 𝒳 = 𝒳₀ ⊗ 𝔽̄_q, and ℓ ≠ p. For every i, H^i(𝒳, ℚ_ℓ) is finite-dimensional and pure of weight i: every eigenvalue of the geometric Frobenius is a Weil q-number of weight i. No global quotient presentation and no condition that ℓ is prime to the stabiliser orders is imposed, since the coefficients are rational. This is a purity statement only; weighted point counts of stacks, rationality of their zeta functions and duality on stacks are not part of it.
hypotheses: 𝒳₀ smooth and proper over 𝔽_q, Deligne–Mumford, of finite type; ℓ invertible.
Coefficients ℚ_ℓ (or ℚ̄_ℓ); with torsion coefficients the comparison with the coarse space fails when ℓ divides a stabiliser order.
proofSteps: Let π : 𝒳₀ → C₀ be the coarse moduli space, a proper algebraic space over 𝔽_q, étale-locally the quotient of a smooth scheme by a finite group (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1). Since the stabilisers are finite and the coefficients are rational, Rπ_*ℚ_ℓ = ℚ_ℓ (invariants under a finite group are exact on ℚ_ℓ-modules), so H^i(C, ℚ_ℓ) → H^i(𝒳, ℚ_ℓ) is a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism (requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1).

C₀ is of pure dimension N on each component and étale-locally a quotient of a smooth scheme by a finite group, so Ra^!ℚ_ℓ ≅ ℚ_ℓ(N)[2N] Frobenius-equivariantly, the hypothesis of DWP.7/hodge-type-triangles-and-proper-smooth-purity-3-3-7-3-3-11 (iii) (Weil II (3.3.11)); applied to the proper C₀ it gives purity of H^i(C, ℚ_ℓ), hence of H^i(𝒳, ℚ_ℓ). The extension of (3.3.11) from schemes to proper algebraic spaces with quotient singularities is the recorded gap on Weil II (3.3.11) for algebraic spaces.
Check for a global quotient [Y/G] with Y smooth proper and G finite: H^i([Y/G], ℚ_ℓ) = H^i(Y_{𝔽̄_q}, ℚ_ℓ)^G is a Frobenius-stable subspace of a pure space, hence pure, even when ℓ divides |G|.
acceptance: For a scheme regarded as a Deligne–Mumford stack the statement is DWP.7/hodge-type-triangles-and-proper-smooth-purity-3-3-7-3-3-11 (i) with constant coefficients.
For [Y/G] with Y smooth proper and G finite, invariants of a pure representation stay pure, even when ℓ divides |G|.

Properness cannot be dropped: the smooth affine curve 𝔾_m (a Deligne–Mumford stack with trivial stabilisers) has H¹(𝔾_m, ℚ_ℓ) = ℚ_ℓ(−1), of weight 2 in degree 1. B𝔾_m is not an example in either direction: it is not Deligne–Mumford, and its cohomology ℚ_ℓ[c] with c of weight 2 in degree 2 happens to be pure.
M̄_{1,1} over 𝔽_q, whose coarse space is the j-line ℙ¹: H⁰ = ℚ_ℓ and H² = ℚ_ℓ(−1), pure of weights 0 and 2, and H¹ = 0.

sources.match: Remarks that smoothness enters the preceding results only through Poincaré duality, so that it may be replaced by the condition Ra^!ℚ_ℓ = ℚ_ℓ(N)[2N], which holds for a scheme étale-locally the quotient of a smooth scheme of dimension N by a finite group. The coarse space of a smooth Deligne–Mumford stack has this local form; that it is an algebraic space rather than a scheme is the recorded gap.

nodes.title: Chebotarev density for finite Galois covers of a curve over 𝔽_q, with constant-field degrees and explicit error
nodes.statement: Let X₀ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g_X over 𝔽_q with function field K, M/K a finite Galois extension with group G, 𝔽_{q^h} the field of constants of M (the algebraic closure of 𝔽_q in M), N = Gal(M/K𝔽_{q^h}) ⊴ G, so that G/N is cyclic of order h generated by the image φ of the q-power arithmetic Frobenius, g_M the genus of M over 𝔽_{q^h}, and R the sum of the degrees of the closed points of X₀ ramified in M. For a conjugacy class C of G and r ≥ 1, let π_C(r) be the number of closed points x of X₀ of degree r, unramified in M, whose arithmetic Frobenius class is C. (i) If C does not map to φ^r in G/N, then π_C(r) = 0. (ii) If C maps to φ^r, then |r·π_C(r) − (#C/#N)(q^r + 1)| ≤ (2g_M + r(1 + 2g_X)) q^{r/2} + r + R. (iii) Hence, for a fixed class C mapping to φ^{r₀}, as r → ∞ through r ≡ r₀ (mod h) the proportion of degree-r closed points of X₀ with Frobenius class C tends to h·#C/#G = #C/#N; for the geometric Frobenius F_x = Frob_x⁻¹ the same holds with C replaced by C⁻¹ and φ^r by φ^{−r}. For a connected finite Galois étale cover of an open U₀ ⊂ X₀ the ramified points lie in X₀ − U₀.
hypotheses: X₀ smooth projective geometrically connected over 𝔽_q; M/K finite Galois (separable); r ≥ 1.

The only arithmetic input is Weil's bound for smooth projective geometrically connected curves over finite fields, applied to the twisted curves of M and to X₀ over 𝔽_{q^d}, d | r; no L-function, no Weil II and no number-field Chebotarev theorem is used.
proofSteps: (i): the Frobenius of a closed point x acts on the constants 𝔽_{q^h} ⊂ M as the q^{deg x}-power map, so its class maps to φ^{deg x} in G/N.

Kosters's parametrisation: for γ ∈ G mapping to the Frobenius of the base, the rational places of K whose Frobenius set contains γ are the images of the rational places of a geometrically irreducible function field M_γ over the base field, the fixed field of the twisted Frobenius (F′, γ) in the constant extension of M, with explicit fibre cardinalities; M_γ has genus g_M (Kosters, arXiv v2 Theorem 1.2 and Lemmas 1.5–1.6; Theorem 1.1 and Lemmas 1.3–1.4 in v1).

Apply this over 𝔽_{q^r} to M𝔽_{q^r}/K𝔽_{q^r}, whose group is the preimage of ⟨φ^r⟩ in G and whose geometric group is N, and use Weil's bound for M_γ (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.7/weight-weil-estimate-for-curves): the number of points of X₀(𝔽_{q^r}) unramified in M with Frobenius in C differs from (#C/#N)(q^r + 1) by at most 2g_M q^{r/2} + R, summing Kosters's estimate for one element (v2 Corollary 1.3, v1 Corollary 1.2; the sum there runs over the rational places) over the elements γ ∈ C, each of which maps to φ^r, and using #C ≤ #N for the genus term. An unramified rational place with Frobenius class C contributes exactly 1 to the sum over γ ∈ C of its Frobenius measure, and a ramified one at most 1, so the ramified places change the count by at most R.

A closed point of degree r gives r points of X₀(𝔽_{q^r}), all with Frobenius in its class; points over closed points of degree d | r, d ≤ r/2, number at most Σ_{d ≤ r/2} #X₀(𝔽_{q^d}) ≤ r((1 + 2g_X) q^{r/2} + 1) by Weil's bound for X₀. Subtract and use #C ≤ #N to get (ii); (iii) follows because the error is O(q^{r/2}) while the main term is (#C/#N) q^r.
acceptance: Constant extension M = K𝔽_{q^h}: G = ℤ/h, N = 1, and the only class occurring in degree r is φ^r, with r·π_{φ^r}(r) = r·(number of degree-r closed points) ≈ q^r.
h = 1 (M/K geometric): the main coefficient is #C/#G, the classical density.
Quadratic geometric extension y² = f(x) of 𝔽_q(x), q odd, with f squarefree of degree 2g + 1: G = N = ℤ/2, and the split and inert degree-r places each have proportion tending to 1/2.
For U₀ = 𝔾_m and the Kummer cover t ↦ t^m (m | q − 1): the cover is a constant-field-trivial cyclic extension ramified at 0 and ∞, so R = 2 and every class of ℤ/m has density 1/m.

sources.match: Parametrises the rational places with a given Frobenius element by the rational places of a geometrically irreducible twisted function field, and deduces over a finite field, for one element γ of the Frobenius coset, the count of rational places weighted by the Frobenius measure, with main term (q + 1)/#N and error 2g√q/#N; v2 adds that summing over a conjugacy class gives the familiar form. sourceIssues.printed: Statement (c) asserts that if, for one ℓ, the factors P_{r,ℓ} are pairwise coprime then each has integer coefficients; the argument deduces this from the fact that their reciprocal roots are algebraic integers. The proof of (d) then cites (c) for integrality.
sourceIssues.correction: Algebraic-integer reciprocal roots only make the coefficients of P_{r,ℓ} algebraic integers lying in ℚ_ℓ. Rationality needs a Galois-stable description of the roots of P_{r,ℓ} among those of the reduced numerator or denominator, which purity gives (the roots of absolute value q^{r/2}, Weil I, proof of (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), p. 277); then Gauss's lemma gives integer coefficients. So (d) holds by that argument, and (c) is established only once purity is known.
sourceIssues.reason: A factorisation over ℚ_ℓ of an integer polynomial into coprime factors need not be defined over ℚ: for ℓ = 7, 1 − 2t² = (1 − √2 t)(1 + √2 t) with √2 ∈ ℚ_7, and both factors have algebraic-integer reciprocal roots. Coprimality of the P_{r,ℓ} for one ℓ does not exclude such a splitting of the numerator or denominator.
